statement: A spherical balloon is inflated so that its volume increases at a constant rate of $20\,\text{cm}^{3}/\text{s}$. Find the rate at which the radius is increasing when the radius is $10\,\text{cm}$.
solution: $V=\frac43\pi r^{3}$, so $\frac{dV}{dr}=4\pi r^{2}$. Given $\frac{dV}{dt}=20$, we have $\frac{dr}{dt}=\frac{dV/dt}{dV/dr}=\frac{20}{4\pi r^{2}}=\frac{5}{\pi r^{2}}$. At $r=10$, $\frac{dr}{dt}=\frac{5}{\pi\cdot100}=\frac{1}{20\pi}\ \text{cm/s}$.
hints: Differentiate V=(4/3)pi r^3 with respect to r.
